transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (CTO - Harrington), Marta Ruiz (CISO), Owen Patel (Sr. DevOps)

Auto-generated summary (may contain errors):
Customer evaluating Redwood for inference hosting; primary concerns are SOC2 scope, key management, SSO integration, audit log streaming to Splunk, and retention policy for PII. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs; customer leaning to Private but wants cost comparison and architectural notes.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Ortega: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jamie from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:12] Liam Chen: Hi, Liam Chen, CTO at Harrington. We're the team building thermal control firmware analytics, a lot of customer telemetry and some PII hashed into ids.
[00:20] Marta Ruiz: Marta, CISO. I'll be driving compliance questions, SOC2 and ISO mostly.
[00:24] Owen Patel: Owen, I run infra. Curious about network, KMS, how you'd do HSM integration.
[00:31] Priya Raman: Great, thanks. Today we want to map your security requirements to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and note any gaps.
[00:40] Liam Chen: High level - we're leaning to private because of data residency and contractual SLAs, but open to dedicated if cost is prohibitive.
[00:48] Jamie Ortega: Totally understandable. Quick question on SOC2: do you need Redwood's SOC2 Type II report in scope for processor controls or do you also need us to map controls to your ISO audit?
[00:58] Marta Ruiz: Mainly processor controls, but if you have ISO 27001 alignment that's nice to see. We'll need the SOC2 report and a control matrix. We also need to understand evidence retention windows for logs.
[01:12] Owen Patel: On logs - we want audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance. Do you support streaming of audit logs or is it a file drop?
[01:20] Priya Raman: We support event streaming via secure forwarders and can push to customer SIEMs. For Private installs we can also provide direct VPC peering so logs never traverse public internet.
[01:32] Marta Ruiz: Can you describe RBAC? We need least privilege and groups mapped to our IdP.
[01:37] Priya Raman: We have role-based roles with granular permissions per-route and per-model. SAML SSO for org-level access and SCIM provisioning for groups — though SCIM support varies slightly between Hosted and Private; it's fully available on Dedicated and Private.
[01:52] Liam Chen: Does SCIM sync include mapping team-to-role?
[01:55] Priya Raman: Yes, you can sync groups and map to RBAC roles. We noted an early customer had some attribute mapping quirks — the auto-provisioner sometimes maps "dept" differently, so we usually validate in a staging SCIM sync.
[02:08] Marta Ruiz: KMS - we need CMEK with customer-managed keys. Also HSM-backed if possible for higher assurance.
[02:15] Jamie Ortega: For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys; for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS. Private supports HSM integrations and external key stores via a KMS proxy.
[02:29] Owen Patel: Can we rotate keys without service disruption?
[02:33] Priya Raman: Yes, key rotation is supported and we've done blue/green rotations. For Private the rotation plan depends on your KMS but we provide a rotation handler.
[02:44] Liam Chen: Data residency - we need all inference logs and KV cache to live in EU exclusively for certain customers.
[02:52] Priya Raman: We can pin region for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has region hints but not hard guarantees unless you opt into a region-specific tenancy. We should capture which APIs and log sinks are in scope.
[03:05] Marta Ruiz: Retention - legal wants 7 years for certain telemetry, but the engineering team wants to prune after 90 days. Is there per-tenant retention policies?
[03:14] Jamie Ortega: Yes, retention is configurable per-customer in Private and Dedicated. Hosted has company-level retention settings with longer-term archive options. We can support tiered retention with archival to S3 and lifecycle policies.
[03:26] Owen Patel: About audit logs - what falls into audit log vs usage metrics vs trace? We need admin actions, model version rollouts, API keys creation, and all token-level access in the audit log.
[03:38] Priya Raman: Audit logs include admin actions, user authentication events, model actions (deploy, rollback), and request metadata. For token-level content we scrub sensitive payloads; full request bodies can be optionally captured in Private if policy allows.
[03:51] Marta Ruiz: Scrubbing - can you redact PII automatically?
[03:55] Priya Raman: We provide pattern-based redaction and can integrate a post-processing step. For high-assurance flows we recommend pre-send redaction or a private deployment.
[04:05] Liam Chen: On-boarding timeline - procurement wants security docs fast. Do you have any standard security package?
[04:11] Jamie Ortega: Yes, we'll send SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, ISO alignment notes, network diagrams, and our whitepaper on KMS options. I'll follow up after the call.
[04:19] Owen Patel: About network - for Private will you require transit VPC or do you support customer-managed firewall with address ranges?
[04:27] Priya Raman: We support both. For Private we usually do VPC peering with route tables and security groups; we can also do private link / transit gateway depending on cloud provider.
[04:36] Marta Ruiz: Who has access to logs inside Redwood operations team? Need to know people, roles, and break-glass procedures.
[04:43] Priya Raman: Access is limited to SREs with RBAC controls and just-in-time access with audit trails. Break-glass requires two-person approval and is logged. We'll produce the access matrix.
[04:55] Liam Chen: Any third-party subprocessors we should flag?
[04:59] Jamie Ortega: Standard cloud providers and monitoring vendors. We'll include a subprocessors list in the compliance pack.
[05:06] Marta Ruiz: Encryption at rest - are data and KV cache encrypted with the same key as objects?
[05:12] Priya Raman: Objects (blobs) and KV stores can use separate key scopes. In Private you can define key hierarchy: master key in KMS -> envelope keys for stores. In Hosted we manage keys by default.
[05:25] Owen Patel: For Dedicated: performance vs cost - do we see different batching/kv-cache behavior?
[05:31] Priya Raman: Dedicated allows you to tune batching and larger KV caches. That's part of Redwood Optimize. We can show performance deltas in the next session.
[05:41] Liam Chen: If we choose dedicated with VPC peering, can we still have dedicated hardware in region EU-West-1?
[05:47] Jamie Ortega: Yes, we can reserve capacity regionally. We'll include availability zones and latency SLOs in the pricing pack.
[05:56] Marta Ruiz: Audit log retention - can we set separate retention for admin logs vs inference request logs?
[06:01] Priya Raman: Yes, different retention classes supported. Admin logs typically retained longer by default. You can tier inference logs to hot, warm, cold.
[06:10] Owen Patel: Does Redwood provide an immutable audit store or can we forward to our write-once storage?
[06:15] Priya Raman: We can forward to your write-once S3 bucket or a WORM-compliant archive. For Private installs you can host the archive.
[06:23] Marta Ruiz: Pen test - do you do internal or third-party pentests and do you share the findings?
[06:28] Jamie Ortega: We do annual third-party pen tests and will share high-level findings and remediation summaries; raw reports can be shared under NDA.
[06:36] Liam Chen: Can you FIPS-140 validate the crypto modules if we need that?
[06:41] Priya Raman: FIPS is complex — we can support FIPS-validated HSMs in Private. Hosted default crypto isn't FIPS certified. We'll flag the difference in the docpack.
[06:51] Owen Patel: SCIM provisioning quirks - any known IdPs with issues?
[06:55] Priya Raman: A couple of older Okta versions needed mapping patches. We maintain a compatibility matrix and can run a test sync in staging.
[07:06] Marta Ruiz: We need to show our auditors how Redwood supports data subject requests and right-to-be-forgotten flows.
[07:13] Jamie Ortega: For Private we can implement delete hooks to remove PII from stores and invalidate KV cache; for Hosted we have delete APIs and retention controls but might require longer caveats for immutable audit trails.
[07:26] Liam Chen: What about e-discovery/legal holds?
[07:29] Priya Raman: We support preservation modes that freeze retention policies. For Private you can snapshot and export with cryptographic proof.
[07:37] Owen Patel: Network encryption - TLS versions supported?
[07:40] Priya Raman: We support TLS 1.2+ and prefer 1.3. Mutual TLS is available for service-to-service connections in Private.
[07:49] Marta Ruiz: Do you have an ATO playbook or something we can plug into our procurement checklist?
[07:53] Jamie Ortega: We'll provide a procurement checklist with required docs and contacts, plus a sample ATO flow.
[08:01] Liam Chen: Who signs the DPIA or data processing addendum?
[08:05] Jamie Ortega: Our legal team signs the DPA; we'll attach the standard template but can negotiate specific clauses for data residency and processor subcontracts.
[08:15] Owen Patel: SLAs for log delivery and ingestion - what are they?
[08:19] Priya Raman: For Dedicated/Private we can back SLAs for log ingestion latency and durability. Hosted has best-effort for certain log paths. We'll include numbers.
[08:28] Liam Chen: How granular is cost reporting? I want cost per-token per-route.
[08:33] Jamie Ortega: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-model, per-route dashboards. We'll include a sample export for your finance team.
[08:42] Marta Ruiz: On key rotation again - do you have automated rotation or manual? For compliance we need a rotation schedule and proof.
[08:49] Priya Raman: Automated rotation supported with rotation events logged and rotation attestations available in Private.
[08:56] Liam Chen: For Private deployment, what infra do you need from our side? VPC, subnets, route tables, maybe an IAM role?
[09:03] Priya Raman: Correct — we'll request VPC with specific subnets, IGW disabled for private subnets, peering or TGW config, and an IAM role for cross-account KMS access if present. We'll share a checklist.
[09:13] Owen Patel: Any expected outage for migration if we switch from Hosted to Private?
[09:18] Jamie Ortega: Migrations can be planned with cutover windows; we usually do a warm sync and redirect traffic during a short cutoff to minimize downtime.
[09:27] Marta Ruiz: Regulatory - do you have any customers in regulated verticals similar to us?
[09:31] Jamie Ortega: Yes, we've worked with medtech and payments customers. We'll share anonymized case studies and their compliance architectures.
[09:40] Liam Chen: Alright, let's recap next steps...
[09:44] Jamie Ortega: Recap - we'll send compliance pack (SOC2, pen test, ISO notes), procure a subprocessors list, deliver Private deployment checklist and sample architecture. Priya will draft VPC diagram and KMS options. Owen will send current retention policy.
[09:58] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. I'll expect the SOC2 and pen test by Friday.
[10:02] Jamie Ortega: Thanks all, we'll follow up with an email and schedule the deep-dive.
[10:06] <end of auto transcript - timestamps approximate, transcription may contain errors>
